name: Foils/wraps
anchor: EU food-contact framework Regulation 1935/2004 with Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II specific migration limits as the only element-migration instrument in the register expressed in the food-contact FOOD basis (the register's other migration instruments — the EU 2009/48 toy Categories I to III and the ASTM F963 soluble limits — are in the toy article-extraction basis and are barred from every row of this category). Rows whose principal food-contact surface is a polymer anchor it directly, or by disclosed read-across where the instrument's own scope article excludes or does not reach the material or where the taxonomy row also carries a non-plastic configuration. Metal, alloy, ceramic-glaze, vitreous-enamel and glass rows, and the two water-treatment-device rows, are controls because their dedicated release regimes (Directive 84/500/EEC as amended by 2005/31/EC, the metals-and-alloys release regime, and the drinking-water device route) are not in the register in their own jurisdictions' rows. Where one taxonomy row carries both a polymer and a metal configuration, the published cells take the metal-article control and the plastics value is disclosed as a film-only companion.
native_basis: element release from the food-contact surface into food or food simulant (ug/kg food), reported separately for the polymeric-film and the rolled-aluminium-foil configuration
native_basis_label: element RELEASE FROM THE FOOD-CONTACT SURFACE INTO FOOD OR A FOOD SIMULANT, ug/kg of food, determined against acidic and salted simulants at the maximum contact temperature and duration claimed on the pack. The row's PUBLISHED cells are expressed in the METAL-ARTICLE release basis, because one of this row's two configurations is rolled aluminium foil, whose food-contact surface is the element itself and which has no polymeric food-contact surface at all. The Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex III to V plastics-simulant convention governs only the polymeric cling and barrier-film configuration and appears on this row as a disclosed COMPANION obligation, never as the published ceiling for the metal article. This is a RELEASE basis on the food and never a total-content basis: no cell on this row limits how much of an element the material CONTAINS, and no cell is expressed per kg of material.
scope_note: Two material configurations sit in one taxonomy row and this record holds them apart rather than pooling them. The polymeric cling and barrier-wrap configuration is a material consisting exclusively of plastics and is directly within Reg (EU) 10/2011. The ROLLED ALUMINIUM FOIL configuration is not: it is a metal article whose food-contact surface is the element itself, metals and alloys are a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, and no credible sovereign sets an element release ceiling for a metal foil. Because one taxonomy row can carry only one published provenance, EVERY published cell on this row now takes the METAL-ARTICLE RELEASE CONTROL regime used on cookware-metal-alloy and utensils-metal, and the corresponding Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II value is disclosed as that cell's COMPANION obligation, binding the polymeric-film configuration only and verified on every film lot. This is exactly the treatment aluminium already received on this row, and the reason generalises to every element on the panel: applying a plastics specific migration limit to rolled aluminium foil asserts of an article made of the element a number written for a polymer surface, which is a misapplication rather than a conservative reading, and aluminium foil in contact with acidic and salted food is documented to exceed it. Extending the carve-out to the whole panel moves in the conservative direction, because it declines to publish a ceiling one configuration cannot meet rather than declining to be strict, and it removes the internal contradiction of a record that made the misapplication argument for one element while publishing the misapplication for six. The film and foil configurations are tested, reported and certified separately and are never pooled. Splitting this taxonomy row into a polymeric-wrap row and an aluminium-foil row, each with its own native basis and its own provenance, is the cleaner fix and is recorded as a taxonomy change for governance rather than taken unilaterally here.
material: Two configurations in one taxonomy row: polymeric cling and barrier wrap (LDPE, PVC, PVDC, polyolefin cling film) and rolled aluminium foil, plain or paper-backed.
components: Sample and report separately: (1) polymeric cling or barrier film food-contact surface, including plasticiser-bearing PVC cling; (2) aluminium foil bright side and matt side, tested against acidic and salted simulant at the contact temperature claimed on the pack; (3) paper backing of backed foil, where product can reach it; (4) any printed or coated foil surface; (5) core or dispenser cutting edge where it can shed onto product.
basis_guard: specific migration into food|element release|specific release|release into food|release into a food simulant|release into the food simulant|acetic acid
basis_guard_note: This row carries two material configurations, so the guard admits BOTH the metal-article release basis in which the row's published cells are expressed and the Reg (EU) 10/2011 specific-migration-into-food basis in which its film-only companion obligations are expressed. It admits nothing else. The guard exists to reject the three foreign bases that surround this category and would otherwise look plausible: the FOOD basis (canned-food tin maximum levels, which limit the contents and not the article), the MATERIAL-CONTENT basis (CPSIA total lead in substrate, EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium percent-by-weight restrictions, RoHS homogeneous-material limits, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals), and the ARTICLE-EXTRACTION basis of the toy regime (EU 2009/48 Annex II Part III and ASTM F963 soluble limits, which are element migration from scraped-off or coated TOY material into 0.07 M hydrochloric acid, expressed per kg of MATERIAL, not per kg of food). Any of those would fail this guard and resolve to a gap rather than publish in the wrong basis.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact product form expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant; a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign value in the same basis where the food-contact material family is expressly excluded from or not reached by that instrument; a substantiated not-material determination; or a control. No cell is occurrence-derived, and no cell borrows a value across a basis.

Pb.rationale: No sovereign sets a food-RELEASE (migration) lead limit for bare-metal food-contact articles in the register. The KR MFDS metal-FCM value is an alloy-COMPOSITION spec (percent by weight), not a release-into-food limit, so it is not adopted here. Proper source: China GB 4806.9-2016 metal-FCM migration limits / CoE CM/Res(2013)9 (pending addition to the register).

Al.rationale: Aluminium on this row is a control, and the carve-out is deliberate. The polymeric-film configuration is bound by the EU 10/2011 Annex II aluminium specific migration limit of 1 mg/kg food, which is disclosed as this cell's companion and is verified on every film lot. The ALUMINIUM-FOIL configuration is not: rolled aluminium foil is a metal article whose food-contact surface is aluminium itself, metals and alloys are a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, and no credible sovereign sets an aluminium release ceiling for a metal foil. Publishing the plastics SML against aluminium foil would take a number written for a polymer surface and assert it of an article made of the element, which is a misapplication rather than a conservative reading, and it is documented that aluminium foil in contact with acidic or salted food exceeds it. HMTc therefore mandates release testing of the foil configuration under the declared contact conditions with no invented ceiling, and reports the film and foil configurations separately rather than pooling them.
Al.reference_method: Food-simulant release testing on each food-contact metal component under worst foreseeable use conditions (acidic simulant at the article's stated cooking or holding temperature and duration; for repeat-use articles the third successive release result governs), ICP-MS determination in the simulant, plus alloy-composition verification of every food-contact component by ICP-OES after acid digestion (XRF for screening only). Foil tested against 3 percent acetic acid and against a salted simulant at the maximum contact temperature and duration claimed on the pack, reporting bright and matt sides separately.

companions.basis: specific migration into food; source unit mg/kg food

Cr.rationale: This taxonomy row covers two material configurations and the published cell governs both, so it is a control. The polymeric cling and barrier-film configuration is bound by the Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II value disclosed as this cell's COMPANION, which is a mandatory obligation verified on every film lot. The ROLLED ALUMINIUM FOIL configuration is not bound by it: foil is a metal article whose food-contact surface is the element itself, metals and alloys are a Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, and no credible sovereign - EU, UK, Codex, US, AU-NZ, Canada or Hong Kong - sets an element release ceiling for a metal foil. Publishing the plastics value against aluminium foil would take a number written for a polymer surface and assert it of an article made of the element, which is a misapplication rather than a conservative reading. That is the reasoning this row already applied to aluminium, and it holds identically for every other element on the panel, so the whole panel takes the metal-article release control used on cookware-metal-alloy and utensils-metal rather than a plastics anchor. Testing is mandatory on every certified lot with no invented ceiling, and the film and foil configurations are reported separately and never pooled. Total chromium is retained as a mandatory determination on both configurations. On the film configuration the companion is the Annex II point 2 non-detect branch, and HMTc declines the 3.6 mg/kg food relaxation that Reg (EU) 2020/1245 makes available on documented exclusion of chromium(VI), so the film companion is the hexavalent-conservative form of the requirement. On the foil configuration no sovereign release ceiling exists, chromate-conversion and passivation treatments are live pathways, and total chromium is a screening determination whose health-relevant species cell is separately controlled.
Cr.reference_method: Food-simulant release testing on each food-contact surface under worst foreseeable use conditions. The FOIL configuration is tested against 3 percent acetic acid and against a salted simulant at the maximum contact temperature and duration claimed on the pack, reporting bright and matt sides separately, with alloy-composition verification of the foil by ICP-OES after acid digestion (XRF for screening only). The FILM configuration is tested per EN 1186 / EN 13130 with simulant, temperature and contact time selected per Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex III and Annex V against its companion value. ICP-MS determination of the element in the simulant in both cases, reported separately by configuration.
